raw_response:
I farm only 2 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs me real money, but if I cut too much and the yield falls, that loss is worse. I have done wheat-maize for many years, and here in Quzhou County most people do about the same kind of management. I do not like making big changes. I start from what worked before and adjust a little. Since I have well irrigation, I will not let the crop suffer for water if it turns dry. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the main fertilizer in before sowing, then add nitrogen once at jointing. Wheat needs steady growth, so I will give enough nitrogen, some phosphorus, and a little potassium. For maize after wheat, I will still use hybrid seed because the yield is better and most people around me use it. Maize eats fertilizer hard, especially nitrogen, so I will not be stingy there. I will do rotary tillage because my land is small and that is the easiest and cheapest way for me. For pesticides, I will not spray too many times, only when the field usually needs it: wheat for weeds and disease or aphids, maize for weeds and then armyworm or aphids if they come. If prices are not too high, I will keep fertilizer a little on the safe side rather than risk a bad harvest.
